headline: No sign of hacking appears in the nationwide FAA ground stop, and the FBI has turned to a software update as the likely cause.

emerging_trends.text: Vendors' own code now rivals intruders as a cause of national disruption: the FBI is examining a software update behind the FAA ground stop, days after a bad update crashed Microsoft 365 around the world.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FAA Ground Stop Points to a Software Update

emerging_trends.text: The guarantees customers buy to keep an untrusted operator out of their data cracked twice this week, as Mior and Skyfall read and rewrote memory inside AMD SEV-SNP virtual machines and an implanted circuit board copied recovery phrases off the screen of Trezor Safe 5 wallets.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Mior and Skyfall Crack AMD SEV-SNP

emerging_trends.text: Criminal crews have moved automation into the back office of their operations, with ArcticRAT running stolen Android data through analysis that ranks each victim by wealth while a WARDEN Stealer loader rides a Google Colab notebook promising a GTA 6 download.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ArcticRAT Scores Victims While a Fake GTA 6 Drops WARDEN

topics.title: FAA Ground Stop Points to a Software Update
topics.latest_developments: Federal officials say no evidence of a cyberattack sits behind the nationwide Federal Aviation Administration communications failure that grounded departures, and the FBI is reportedly examining a software update as the trigger, after the agency first attributed the ground stop to extraordinary circumstances and named no cause.
topics.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted flights across the United States when its communications broke down, and airlines and passengers absorbed the delays. The agency has yet to publish the faulty component, the vendor, or a repair timeline.

sources.title: No Signs of Hacking in FAA Ground Stop as FBI Reportedly Probes Software Update
FAA Ground Stop Issued Due to 'Extraordinary Circumstances'

topics.title: Attackers Take Commands on UnrealIRCd Servers
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-114713 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Friday, November 13, 2026 after reports of active exploitation, and the flaw's mechanism came into focus: improper neutralization of delimiters, rated 8.6, hands an attacker command injection at the server level.
topics.summary: UnrealIRCd runs open-source Internet Relay Chat servers, many of them on long-lived Linux hosts that administrators rarely revisit. Operators should upgrade now, and federal civilian agencies face a remediation deadline under the KEV listing.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection

topics.title: Implants Ride Trezor Safe 5 Wallets From a Reseller
topics.latest_developments: Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 devices sold by CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller, carry an extra circuit board that reads the wallet's recovery phrase off its screen and sends the phrase over the cellular network to a server the attackers control, and the company released a fix.
topics.summary: Trezor examined one of the wallets in its lab and identified the other two. Anyone holding a Safe 5 bought through CryptoBilis should apply Trezor's fix and move funds to a new recovery phrase generated on a device bought direct.

sources.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases

topics.title: ArcticRAT Scores Victims While a Fake GTA 6 Drops WARDEN
topics.latest_developments: ArcticRAT, the Android malware, has grown past cryptocurrency theft into full device control and now runs the data it steals through analysis that profiles each victim's finances, and Cynet researchers followed a Google Colab notebook advertising a GTA 6 executable to a ZIP archive holding a WARDEN Stealer loader that takes saved passwords, browser cookies, Steam and Roblox credentials, and cryptocurrency wallet data.
topics.summary: Both campaigns chase consumer money through the device rather than the bank. Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19, 2026 with no PC version, so every site offering a PC download is bait; blocking unsigned executables and steering staff off game-crack sites closes the WARDEN route.

sources.title: ArcticRAT Cybercrime Gang Profiles Victim Finances With AI
Fake GTA 6 download goes after Steam logins and crypto wallet data

topics.title: Mior and Skyfall Crack AMD SEV-SNP
topics.latest_developments: Researchers published two attacks this week, Mior and Skyfall, that let the operator of a server read data inside AMD SEV-SNP virtual machines, with Mior also modifying a guest's memory and forging the signed attestation report that tells a customer which software the machine runs.
topics.summary: AMD SEV-SNP underpins confidential computing at the major clouds, where it promises that the host cannot see a tenant's data. Both attacks require control of the hypervisor and Mior also requires control of the BIOS, which places the risk on malicious or compromised hosting providers.

sources.title: New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs

topics.title: New York City Bars Surveillance Pricing
topics.latest_developments: The New York City Council passed a bill that lets the city fine a company $1,000 for each verified instance of surveillance pricing, the practice of setting a shopper's price from that shopper's personal data, as comparable bans gain ground in other jurisdictions.
topics.summary: Retailers and platforms that tune prices to an individual's browsing history, location, or device now face per-instance penalties in the largest city in the United States. Companies selling into New York should audit what personal signals their pricing engines consume.

sources.title: NYC to bar surveillance pricing as momentum for bans grows nationwide

business_politics.title: Trump Calls Xi and Putin to Shenzhen
business_politics.latest_developments: The Wall Street Journal reported late Friday, November 13, that President Trump will sit down with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together next week in Shenzhen, and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday, November 14, that Washington has floated NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for a Ukrainian withdrawal from the Donbas.
business_politics.summary: A three-way meeting of the American, Chinese, and Russian leaders would be the first of its kind, and it follows the Abu Dhabi rounds that produced a prisoner exchange and no ceasefire. Zelenskyy says he will put the Donbas-for-NATO proposal to Ukrainians; European capitals warn that reopening the alliance's membership question before any ceasefire hands Moscow leverage over the continent's whole security order.

sources.title: Trump to Hold Talks With China's Xi and Russia's Putin Next Week
US floats Nato membership for Donbas withdrawal deal, Zelenskyy says
Europe Express: opening a security can of worms

business_politics.title: Central Banks Lean Toward Bigger Increases
business_politics.latest_developments: Federal Reserve policymakers have floated a larger rate increase at the December meeting after strong jobs, growth, and inflation data, the Financial Times reported Saturday, November 14, and Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill told the paper the same morning that British borrowing costs have "further to go."
business_politics.summary: A half-point move in December would mark the Fed's largest increase since 2022 and would follow the hot October consumer price reading that drove two-year Treasury yields up and pushed the 10-year past 5%. Pill called the Bank of England's quarter-point increase to 4% last week a "significant step" toward beating inflation, signaling more rises in the United Kingdom as well.

sources.title: Hawkward timing
BoE chief economist says further rate rises needed to combat inflation
Transcript of an interview with Huw Pill

business_politics.title: The Ground Stop's Weekend Tail
business_politics.latest_developments: The Federal Aviation Administration lifted its nationwide ground stop after roughly four hours late Friday, November 13, the Trump administration blamed "overloaded" systems, and the Transportation Department now asks Congress for $50 billion to rebuild American air traffic control, a job one official likened to changing a tire at 70 miles an hour.
business_politics.summary: Communications failures at regional air traffic control centers halted every departing United States flight Friday afternoon, and airlines expect delays and cancellations to run through the weekend as crews and aircraft land out of position. The shutdown scrambled college and professional sports travel and left thousands of passengers hunting for hotel rooms and rental cars.

sources.title: US aviation regulator lifts order that grounded thousands of flights
US plan to overhaul air traffic control system like 'changing a tyre at 70mph'
Weekend Air Travel Woes Mount After FAA Lifts Nationwide Groundstop
Passengers face widespread disruption after US air traffic control outage

business_politics.title: Nvidia's Legal Exposure After Huang
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Saturday, November 14, that Nvidia carries incomplete insurance against damages arising from executive conduct, leaving the chipmaker open to litigation over Jensen Huang's removal, and the Wall Street Journal published an account of the Chinese intelligence operation that American officials believe ensnared him.
business_politics.summary: Nvidia's board ousted Huang this week after he confirmed affairs that included a relationship with an executive whom United States intelligence identified as a Chinese recruit, and finance chief Colette Kress runs the company while directors search for a permanent successor. Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and other founders attacked the decision, likening it to Apple's firing of Steve Jobs, and the FT faulted the board's claim to independence.

sources.title: Nvidia exposed to possible lawsuits after Jensen Huang's downfall
Behind the Nvidia Affair Sits a Vast Chinese Spying Machine
In Jensen Huang's Ouster, Tech Billionaires See a Mistake—and a Lesson
The Nvidia board's artificial independence

business.title: Family Dollar Settles for $63 Million
business.latest_developments: WPXI reported Saturday, November 14, that Family Dollar will pay $63 million, that the Federal Trade Commission and 17 states filed their case in federal court Thursday, November 12, and that a judge must still approve the deal.
business.summary: The FTC complaint says Family Dollar rang up shoppers at prices above those posted on its shelves, website, and mobile app, and that customers across the country reported the practice. Pennsylvania ranks among the states in the case, and Pennsylvanians can claim refunds.

sources.title: Family Dollar to pay $63 million to settle allegations that it routinely overcharged customers

business.title: Pittsburgh International's Terminal Turns One
business.latest_developments: TribLive marked the first anniversary of Pittsburgh International Airport's new terminal Saturday, November 14, with an account of the machinery behind it, including a baggage system whose predecessor ran loud enough that workers risked hearing damage if they pulled out their earplugs.
business.summary: The Allegheny County Airport Authority opened the new terminal a year ago, consolidating ticketing, security, and baggage handling in one building and ending the shuttle trip between the old landside and airside structures. The anniversary lands in the same week the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop halted departures from the airport.

sources.title: Pittsburgh International Airport's new terminal celebrates 1st anniversary

around_town.title: Measles Kills a Seventh Pennsylvanian
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania Department of Health confirmed Saturday, November 14, that a seventh state resident has died of measles this year, out of 1,542 confirmed cases across 46 of the commonwealth's 67 counties.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania's outbreak has now run through two-thirds of its counties and produced the state's largest measles case count in decades. Health officials continue to press parents on vaccination as the case total climbs through the fall.

sources.title: 7th Pennsylvania resident dies from measles, state health officials say

around_town.title: The Season's First Flakes Fly
around_town.latest_developments: Flurries and snow showers crossed Western Pennsylvania before dawn Saturday, November 14, mixing with rain closer to Pittsburgh, and WPXI expects everything to turn to plain rain by mid-morning as temperatures climb toward 40 degrees, with lake effect showers continuing all day and night from the city northward.
around_town.summary: WTAE calls the morning the first flakes of the season and warns that a blink will miss them; nothing sticks below the highest elevations. KDKA's Mary Ours holds chilly air and a light wintry mix over the region through the weekend.

sources.title: Early morning snow flurries switch to rain that continues all day
Western PA: Lake effect rain and snow today
Chilly weather returns to Pittsburgh this weekend, light wintry mix also possible

around_town.title: Greensburg Waits on the Moose Building
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Saturday, November 14, that Greensburg code enforcement officers have cited the former Moose building three times since 2021 for parts of the structure that need repairs, and that the city has received no repair plan from its owner.
around_town.summary: The code violation documents TribLive obtained cover five years of notices on the vacant social hall, a prominent piece of the Westmoreland County seat's downtown. Greensburg's enforcement file now sets up the question of what the city does next with a building nobody has moved to fix.

sources.title: Owner of former Greensburg social hall hasn't offered repair plan, city says

events.title: The Lawrenceville Cat Crawl Runs Today
events.latest_developments: The Lawrenceville Cat Crawl and a Craft-a-Thon, which lead NEXTpittsburgh's weekend guide of more than 15 things to do, both happen today, Saturday, November 14.
events.summary: The Cat Crawl sends visitors through Lawrenceville businesses and cat-centered stops along Butler Street, and NEXTpittsburgh's list runs through Sunday, November 15, with fall celebrations, art openings, film festivals, and theater productions around Pittsburgh.

sources.title: 15+ things to do this weekend, from the Lawrenceville Cat Crawl to a Craft-a-Thon

around_teams.title: Run the Ball, Keep Burrow Off the Field
around_teams.latest_developments: Merril Hoge's Playbook, posted Friday, November 13, argues the Steelers slow Joe Burrow by running the football and controlling the clock, and SNR Drive's Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler made their predictions the same evening with Missi Matthews calling into the show.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh plays the Cincinnati Bengals Sunday, November 15, at 8:20 p.m. Eastern on NBC, an AFC North game the Steelers enter off their bye. The team posted Friday's press conference with T.J. Watt, Derrick Harmon, and Asante Samuel Jr., the last media availability before the trip.

sources.title: Attacking Cincinnati on the ground | Playbook with Merril Hoge | Pittsburgh Steelers
Steelers Vs. Bengals Predictions | SNR Drive (Nov.13) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Tomlin Retells the Jacoby Jones Return
around_teams.latest_developments: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward posted a clip Friday evening, November 13, in which Mike Tomlin tells the hosts what really happened on the Jacoby Jones kickoff return.
around_teams.summary: The clip comes out of the two-part sit-down Cameron Heyward and Hayden recorded with the former Steelers head coach, the same series in which Tomlin explained why he walked away from the job and took his new role at NBC.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: Mike Tomlin tells us what really happened on the Jacoby Jones return 👀#MikeTomlin #Steelers

team_usa.title: Malinin Leads Skate America
team_usa.latest_developments: Ilia Malinin scored 96.74 points Friday, November 13, to lead the men's short program at Skate America, his first Grand Prix outing of the season.
team_usa.summary: Malinin, the American world champion, built the program as a tribute to members of the skating community who died in January 2025 when their American Airlines flight collided with a military helicopter near Washington. He skates the free program for the title with the Milan Cortina Olympics ahead.

sources.title: Malinin leads Skate America after short program tribute to victims of 2025 plane crash

team_usa.title: NWSL Players Press Stadium Operators
team_usa.latest_developments: Players from Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current demanded Saturday, November 14, that stadium operators give women's sports better priority, after venue problems upended both National Women's Soccer League semifinals.
team_usa.summary: Gotham moved its semifinal against Kansas City to Icahn Stadium in New York, a 5,000-seat track facility, because the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey, had deteriorated; players in the earlier round called that surface atrocious. The Washington Spirit's semifinal arrangements drew complaints as well.

sources.title: NWSL players demand more respect for women's sports amid playoff venue issues
